issues.legal_issue: Permission to withdraw a suit with liberty to file a fresh suit at the appellate stage requires careful exercise of discretion based on sufficient grounds, and cannot be granted merely to avoid an adverse finding or on the basis that the defendant will suffer no prejudice.
material_facts: The plaintiffs brought a suit for injunction concerning a proposed flour mill and their claimed exclusive use of a pathway.
The trial court granted relief to the plaintiffs, but the first appellate court held that the pathway was common and could be used by all parties.

The plaintiffs appealed and sought permission to withdraw the suit with liberty to file a fresh suit, saying that they had omitted to seek a declaration of title and that the appellate court’s finding had raised a cloud over their claimed rights.
The High Court granted permission, reasoning in part that the defendants’ use of the pathway could be protected pending adjudication of a fresh suit.

The Supreme Court found that the application was made to overcome the adverse finding and that the High Court had not adequately considered whether sufficient grounds existed or the effect of nullifying the defendants’ benefit from the appellate decision.
issues.conclusion: The High Court’s order granting permission to withdraw the suit with liberty to file a fresh suit was set aside, and the second appeal was to be decided in accordance with law.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order XXIII Rule 1(3) CPC, permission to withdraw a suit with liberty to institute a fresh suit is a discretionary concession, available when the suit must fail because of a formal defect or the court is satisfied that sufficient grounds justify a fresh suit. The court must exercise that discretion cautiously and consider all relevant circumstances, including whether withdrawal would allow an unsuccessful litigant to avoid an adverse decision, nullify an advantage obtained by the defendant, prejudice vested rights, or cause wasteful relitigation. At the appellate stage, the court must apply particular scrutiny; saying that the defendant will not be prejudiced is not by itself sufficient. The Court relied on Bakhatwar Singh v. Soda Kaur, (1996) 11 SCC 167, and Executive Officer, Arthaneswarar Temple v. R. Sathyamoorthy, (1999) 3 SCC 115.

predicates.second_appeal_after_adverse_appellate_fi: The proceeding is a second appeal following an appellate decision that is adverse to the plaintiffs on part of their claim.
predicates.plaintiffs_seek_withdrawal_for_fresh_sui: The plaintiffs seek to withdraw their existing suit so they can bring a fresh suit concerning the same subject matter.
predicates.application_aims_to_overcome_adverse_fin: The plaintiffs seek withdrawal to avoid or overcome an adverse finding made in the existing proceedings.
predicates.court_does_not_assess_sufficient_grounds: The court granting permission does not adequately assess whether sufficient grounds exist and what withdrawal would do to the defendant’s benefit from the existing decision.

issues.definition: When plaintiffs seek to withdraw a suit for fresh litigation after an adverse appellate finding, and the application is aimed at overcoming that finding or the court fails to assess the grounds and effects of withdrawal, the permission is set aside.
